text:
maria-cs: Customer acme-inc on Private VPC (us-west-2) reports multiple model endpoints flapping. ALB target group shows Unhealthy and Envoy logs show TLS handshake failures. Can eng take a look?

ingrid-eng: can you paste the envoy log lines and the ALB health check config? also are they terminating TLS at alb or at envoy?

maria-cs: pasting snippets from customer (sanitized):
```
[2025-10-12T14:22:05Z] [warning] envoy tls error: remote error: tls: handshake failure (tls_handshake.cc:142)
[2025-10-12T14:22:05Z] [debug] ssl: no suitable certificate found for SNI '' (sni_utils.cc:87)
```
ALB target group healthcheck settings: Protocol=HTTPS, Port=traffic-port, Path=/healthz, Interval=10s, Timeout=5s, HealthyThreshold=2, UnhealthyThreshold=2. Listener: TLS on 8443 -> forward to target group.

also customer says they have strict host-based firewall rules (iptables + AWS NACL) and an egress allowlist that only allows traffic to certain IPs.

alex-smith: a few likely things here:
- ALB health check over HTTPS expects TLS handshake; if ALB is doing TLS passthrough vs termination mismatch you'll see SNI/cert issues. Envoy's error about empty SNI indicates ALB healthcheck may not be sending SNI (ALB health checks sometimes don't include Host/SNI).
- If backend expects SNI to select a cert (virtual hosting) and healthcheck doesn't provide it, Envoy will pick no cert -> handshake fails.
- If customer firewall blocks healthcheck source IPs (ALB or internal probes), connection will fail intermittently.

ingrid-eng: reproduce steps to confirm:
1) curl directly to backend instance IP on port 8443 without Host header: `curl -vk https://10.0.12.45:8443/healthz` -> likely shows `alert: tls: handshake failure` or `no certificate matches`
2) curl with Host header matching virtual host/SNI: `curl -vk --resolve api.acme.internal:8443:10.0.12.45 https://api.acme.internal:8443/healthz` -> should succeed if cert present for that host.

maria-cs: customer ran the first curl and got `SSL: no alternative certificate` error. second curl succeeded when they used Host header.

alex-smith: that confirms SNI mismatch. Options:
- Quick mitigation: change ALB health check to use HTTP on the backend listener (terminate TLS at ALB) and use Host header configured in the healthcheck to match the virtual host, or use TCP health check so ALB only checks connect, not TLS.
- Proper fix: configure Envoy to present a default certificate for healthcheck/non-SNI requests (fallback cert) or configure ALB target group healthcheck to send Host header/SNI (ALB may not support SNI for health checks).
- If they have a firewall allowlist: ensure security group attached to instances allows health checks from the ALB security group (recommended), not relying on IP ranges. NACL should allow ephemeral source ports too.

devops-jay: note about AWS specifics: ALBs' healthcheck requests do not set SNI by default; they set Host header only if you explicitly configure it in the target group (TargetGroup -> Health checks -> Host). However ALB health checks over HTTPS may still do a TLS handshake without SNI. If your backend requires SNI -> fail. NLB TCP checks just open socket (no TLS) so they avoid SNI issues.

sre-oncall-bot: [incident-tracker] Incident created INC-2025-1127 for acme-inc private-vpc healthcheck failures. Pager duty: oncall@sre.

ingrid-eng: proposed next steps for customer (ordered):
1) Change target group health check to HTTP on port 80 (or backend HTTP port) with Path=/healthz and set Host to `api.acme.internal` (works if ALB terminates TLS). If termination at Envoy is required, skip to 2.
2) If termination must stay at Envoy on 8443, either:
   - configure Envoy to serve a fallback cert for empty SNI, or
   - switch health check to TCP on the target group so ALB just verifies socket (will not check /healthz content), or
   - put a tiny HTTP listener on 80 that responds 200 at /healthz and set healthcheck to that.
3) Update security groups: allow inbound from ALB SG (reference SG) instead of IPs; remove strict egress blocking that blocks ALB probes or control-plane checks.
4) If customer uses NACLs, ensure return traffic is allowed and ephemeral ports not blocked.
5) Ask customer to run the two curls above and paste outputs.

maria-cs: sent steps to customer and they replied they can temporarily change healthcheck to HTTP and that fixed the flapping (TG shows healthy). They will work on cert fallback next week.

alex-smith: also log for runbook: add a checklist for Private/VPC deployments:
- Ensure target group health check type matches TLS termination (HTTP vs TCP).
- If HTTPS health checks used, verify Host/SNI behavior and provide fallback cert.
- Use SG referencing ALB SGs for health check allowlisting, avoid static AWS IP lists.
- Document curl repro commands in support KB.

maria-cs: customer happy for now. closing loop after they deploy fallback cert. :white_check_mark:
